features.rationale: Turn the annular spacer to nominal finished dimensions; datum A is the end at z = 0.
Both bore mouths are explicitly depicted chamfered in section; apply before cutting the end slot so the front chamfer is interrupted naturally.

Cut the centered twelve-o'clock end slot from datum A; the section establishes axial depth and removal through the radial wall. The rectangle extends into the existing bore to avoid leaving material at its curved boundary.
What size and form of edge break are required on the remaining sharp outside and slot edges?
features.justification: Zero is an unresolved-feature placeholder, not a specified edge-break size; the drawing supplies no size or chamfer-versus-radius instruction.

notes: The full sheet identifies SPACER, drawing 4092-B, model 100TFW, material 1018. The supplied extraction identifier A040921E is retained only as an input-file identifier.

The title block explicitly specifies inches and third-angle projection. General tolerances: two-place dimensions ±.02, three-place dimensions ±.010, angular dimensions ±1°. The bore has its own +.002/-.000 tolerance.

Finished nominal geometry is modeled. The asterisk on 3.000 is resolved by the full-sheet note: '* ALLOW .060 STOCK FOR GR. AT ASSY'. Preserve this as a manufacturing allowance, not an automatic increase of the finished dimension; distribution of grinding stock between end faces is not specified.
The opposite end face is parallel to datum A within D008, per the printed frame '∥ | A | .001'; this is a manufacturing constraint, not an additional geometric feature.
The slot is a single through-wall end notch, not a radial blind keyway. Its width and axial extent are supported jointly by the front view, upper detail, and section.

D009 and D010 are derived extraction values; geometry instead uses the printed diameter and length dimensions directly. No broader application of the .09 chamfer is inferred beyond the two depicted bore mouths.
